Here is a sample Semgrep rule in YAML format for the vulnerability you provided:

```yaml
id: "vuln-dokploy-61cf4266"
type: "regex"
languages: 
  - "typescript"
severity: "ERROR"
message: "Potential exposure of private personal information to unauthorized actor or missing authorization"
description: |
  This rule detects potential exposure of private personal information to an unauthorized actor by not checking if the user is in the same organization before accessing their data.
metadata:
  tags: ["security", "authentication"]
  maturity: "beta"
  cweId: [CWE-359, CWE-862]
  url: "https://semgrep.dev/cves/"
pattern: |
  (?i)
  \b(import|require)\s*\(.*\bdb\.query\.member\.findFirst\(.*\)
  .*
  \b(return|throw)\s*\(.*?\bmemberResult\b.*?;
```

This rule will match any import or require statement that uses `db.query.member.findFirst` and then returns or throws an error without checking if the user is in the same organization. The pattern is case-insensitive, so it can catch both `import` and `require`. 

Please note that this rule might need to be adjusted based on your specific project structure and naming conventions.
